newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rebels kill 49 Algerians in mosque, newspaper says.
newsitem.headline: Rebels kill 49 Algerians in mosque, newspaper says.

text.p: Suspected Moslem rebels broke into a mosque in northern Algeria and slaughtered 49 worshippers kneeling at prayer at the weekend, an Algerian newspaper reported on Tuesday.

El Watan newspaper, quoting witnesses, said the gunmen hacked to death the 49 men with axes and swords on Saturday night in Sidi Abdelaziz village in Medea province, 70 km (40 miles) south of the capital Algiers.
There was no independent confirmation of the report.

The newspaper did not explain why fundamentalist Moslem rebels would kill Moslems at prayer but an El Watan reporter told Reuters that the mosque had been targeted because its preacher was appointed by the government. The reporter said the rebels had also posted leaflets banning Taraouih (evening) prayer in the mosque. It was not clear why.

Sources close to the Algerian security forces told Reuters there had been a massacre in the mosque but gave no details. One source said it was not the first time the rebels had struck a mosque, saying many preachers had been killed.
On Sunday, Algerian security forces said in a statement that 36 people were killed in an attack on Sidi Abdelaziz village the previous night but made no mention of a bloodbath in the mosque.
Liberte newspaper said on Monday that Moslem rebels had killed 48 villagers, including women and children, in Sidi Abdelaziz, but it also made no mention of a mosque attack.
El Watan reported that the leader of the Armed Islamic Group (GIA) had warned in posters stuck on mosques that his rebels would step up attacks during the holy fasting month of Ramadan.

"The war will continue and will be intensified during the month of Ramadan. We have the means and the men to punish all those who are not on our side," GIA leader Antar Zouabri said, quoted by El Watan.
"There is no neutrality in the war we lead. Except for those who are with us, all the others are renegade," Zouabri was quoted as saying.
At least 150 people have been reported killed and more than 170 wounded in Algeria since the start of Ramadan on January 10.
Militant fundamentalists regard the Moslem month of fasting as the month of "jihad" -- holy war -- against the secular military-backed government.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's war since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
A car bomb ripped through a working-class area in Algiers on Sunday evening. The newspaper Liberte on Tuesday put the death toll at 42. The authorities had said 21 people were killed.

Analysts say the killings, often indiscriminate, are a message to President Liamine Zeroual that the fundamentalists are still a formidable force despite repeated claims by the government that it has crushed the guerrillas.
